archetypes.name: awk-template-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The larch-run.sh launcher is written as a single-quoted heredoc; any byte-level divergence between its embedded AWK extraction pattern and the patterns already in pre-bootstrap fences would cause silent root-path mismatch at dispatch time.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the larch-run.sh heredoc in scripts/implement-bootstrap.sh (the `emit_larch_run_sh` function, roughly lines 179–233 of the diff). Compare the embedded `LARCH_CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=` awk extraction line against every existing awk fallback in the pre-bootstrap fence shapes in skills/implement/SKILL.md to confirm they are byte-for-byte identical. Verify that the heredoc delimiter is single-quoted (suppressing host-shell expansion), that all `$script`, `$@`, `${IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR:-}`, and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}` references are intended to expand in the *generated* script rather than the host. Check whether the omission of `set -e` (errexit) alongside `set -uo pipefail` in the emitted launcher leaves any code path that can return non-zero without a matching `exit` call. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: session-transition-safety
archetypes.rationale: Every post-Step-0 fence now hard-depends on `$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/larch-run.sh` existing; sessions in-flight on older tmpdirs at ship time will fail at the first fence, and the quality of that failure message and the routing-envelope propagation of STEP_FAILED=larch-run determines whether operators can recover gracefully.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace what happens when a post-Step-0 fence calls `bash "$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/larch-run.sh"` on a tmpdir that lacks the launcher: does bash produce a clear, diagnosable error or a silent failure? Verify that `STEP_FAILED=larch-run` plus `exit 2` in the fresh-session and resume-tail call sites in scripts/implement-bootstrap.sh are handled by the bootstrap routing envelope parser (parse-bootstrap-routing-envelope.sh or the inline KV block) such that the orchestrator stalls rather than continuing with an empty coder. Check whether the resume-tail emission of larch-run.sh is truly unconditional in the case where `plugin-root.env` already existed (the `if ! emit_larch_run_sh` block appears after the plugin-root sync, but confirm no early-return or guard can skip it). Also examine the duplicate `session write-env --plugin-root-only` retry block (lines 267–274 of the diff) and confirm it is pre-existing rather than a regression introduced by this change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
